title: constraint
content_html:
constraint

In 3 symbols, working in threes and compositing images by a fixed procedure shaped the result alongside practical limits, including the number of folders that fitted on a screen. A choice can begin as an accommodation to a tool and become part of a work’s structure. What would changing one of those constraints have made possible? What distinctive quality might have disappeared with it? 3 symbols

Reading note. Existentialism. In “Freedom and Liberation,” Beauvoir examines what it takes for someone to have actual possibilities for action. Art-making raises a smaller version of that question. Some rules can be changed by the maker. Others come from conditions that determine what choices are available in the first place. The Ethics of Ambiguity, part III, §2
